thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — metering ingestion consumer `usage-emitter` lagging (~12k msgs behind). Token counts are stale and a subset of customers are receiving transient overage flags. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/metering-ingest. Please ack and triage.
maya: acked. jumping in, checking dashboard now.
ben: oncall here. seeing consumer lag on eu-west-1-emitter, consumer group offset stuck at 1,345,200. looks like backpressure from the downstream rate limiter.
maya: yup, dashboard shows emit latency spike at 22:07, emitter CPU 95%. Metrics: `emitter_msgs_inflight` up x3, `token_counter_lag` +11k.
carol: tagging billing and cs: @billing-bot @cs-lead — do we have any immediate customer alerts triggered? can we suppress noisy overage emails while we triage?
billing-bot: We have 127 overage flags generated in last 10m. Auto-notify is ON for prod accounts > threshold. Can temporarily hold notifications via /billing/notifications/pause (admin only).
sre-oncall: suggestion — failover consumer to `usage-emitter-fallback` and scale emitter to +2 replicas. Starting scaledown guardrails.
ben: initiating failover sequence. running:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/usage-emitter -n metering
kubectl scale deployment/usage-emitter --replicas=4 -n metering
# if failover needed
curl -XPOST https://infra.internal/reroute?from=usage-emitter&to=usage-emitter-fallback
```
maya: I'll open a temporary throttle on the billing pipeline to reduce downstream pressure: `billing.rate_limiter.set(0.5)` — will notify when applied.
carol: CS drafting short status note for affected customers: "We’re investigating transient usage reporting delays; if you see an overage alert please ignore — we will reconcile."
ben: rollout restarted, pods are coming up. emitter CPU dropping to 68%.
maya: applied billing throttle. overage notification pause requested to billing-bot: `/billing/notifications/pause 30m`.
billing-bot: notifications paused for 30m by maya. Will hold outbound emails but keep flags in internal UI.
incident-bot: Note: automated backfill job `metering-reconciler` can run to reprocess missed events. Recommend starting once lag <= 0.
ben: consumer offset catching up, currently ~3.2k behind. starting a controlled backfill pre-check to estimate reconciliation cost.
maya: pre-check completed — approx 18k tokens to re-ingest, estimated backfill time 22m. starting backfill now: `jobs run metering-reconciler --start-offset 1345200 --end-offset 1355200`.
carol: CS posting interim message to customers now. keeping it short.
cs-lead: posted template to status.redwood: "We’re experiencing delayed usage reporting for a subset of customers; no billing adjustments have been made yet. We’ll update you within 1 hour."
ben: backfill job started, progress logs: `processed 2k msgs / 18k`.
maya: watching metrics — token counts climbing back toward expected. overage flags should reconcile down as backfill completes.
billing-bot: internal overage flags will be suppressed from external notifications until manual clear. Adding a follow-up task to reconcile and unpause when counts stable.
incident-bot: Incident timeline events: pager 1729518273, failover 1729518430, throttle 1729518501, backfill start 1729518700.
ben: backfill finished at 1729519800. token counts reconciled for most customers. manual sweep in progress for any remaining flags.
maya: confirming: metrics stable, emitter CPU normal, consumer lag 0.
carol: good. CS will send follow-up to customers explaining reconciliation and that no billing adjustments were applied automatically.
cs-lead: sent follow-up. no major customer escalations so far.
ben: closing immediate mitigation. creating postmortem ticket: MR-INC-2026-1729518273 with action items: 1) improve autoscale for usage-emitter, 2) add circuit-breaker to prevent emitter CPU spike, 3) make notification pause runbook easier. assigning to eng-sre and billing.
maya: adding one more action — add synthetic canary that detects token-count divergence greater than 5% and alerts earlier.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 1729520073. Please follow up in the postmortem doc and tag the oncall rotation for retro.
ben: thanks team. :thumbsup:\n
